identity.name: Protectorate General to Pacify the West
identity.wikipedia: Protectorate General to Pacify the West

land.text: Gaochang, conquered 19 September 640 and made Xi Prefecture, seat of the protectorate from 11 October 640
the Tarim oasis states of the Four Garrisons and, after Su Dingfang's victory of 657, the Western Turkic lands

predecessors.note: The oasis kingdoms (Kucha 648-649, Karasahr 648) were taken from their own kings and their Western Turkic overlords.

land.text: 'The Tibetan Empire conquered Qiuci' in 787 and 'Yutian' in 792; the Four Garrisons later passed to Qocho (Karasahr and Kucha, 843), the Kara-Khanids (Kashgar) and a free Khotan (851)

successors.note: Most sources date the protectorate's final collapse 'by 790'; the conquest of Yutian is 792.

capitals.name: Xi Prefecture (Gaochang)
capitals.note: 'Xi Prefecture became the seat of the Anxi Protectorate on 11 October' 640.

capitals.name: Qiuci (Kucha)
capitals.note: 'In 648, the Tang conquered Kucha ... and made it the new seat of Anxi'.

capitals.name: Xi Prefecture (Gaochang)
capitals.note: 'In 651 the seat was moved back to Xi Prefecture'.

capitals.name: Qiuci (Kucha)
capitals.note: 'In 658 the seat was moved back to Qiuci after Su Dingfang defeated the Western Turkic Khaganate'.

capitals.name: Suyab (Suiye)
capitals.note: 'The protectorate's seat was moved to Suyab ... in modern Kyrgyzstan' in 670.

capitals.name: Qiuci (Kucha)
capitals.note: Wang Xiaojie 'established the Anxi Protectorate at Qiuci, where it would remain until the protectorate's demise around 790'. The same page has 'the Tibetan Empire conquered Qiuci' in 787 (the 787 loss, after which the keyframes leave Kucha out), so the seat is ended at 786; the page's 'around 790' and the monk Wukong's 789 account of Chinese commanders still in place are the other reading (reviewer ea-04-x).

correction.text: Gaochang (Turfan), made Xi Prefecture and the seat of the protectorate

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'On 19 September 640 Hou Junji of Tang conquered Gaochang and set up Xi Prefecture'; the protectorate's first land is the Turfan oasis. The 120 km circle is the researcher's reading. The page gives no area.

correction.text: the Tarim Basin under the Four Garrisons (Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, Karasahr) plus Xi Prefecture

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The Four Garrisons of Anxi in Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, and Karashahr were installed between 648 and 658'; 'By 650 the entire Western Region had submitted to Tang authority'. The page draws no frontier.

correction.text: the Tarim Basin and Xi Prefecture plus the Western Turkic lands of Dzungaria and Semirechye after 657

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'By the end of the 657 campaign, the Tang had reached its largest extent.' The page names neither Dzungaria nor Semirechye; they are the researcher's reading of the khaganate's annexation. The protectorate's vassals west of the Pamirs are ledger vassal events, not drawn here.

correction.text: Xi Prefecture, Dzungaria and Semirechye after the Tarim fell to the Tibetans; the seat moved to Suyab

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. In 670 'a Western Turkic tribe allied with the Tibetan Empire invaded the Tarim Basin' and the Tang 'withdrew to Turfan' (Western Turks page); the seat moved to Suyab (Anxi page). Whether Dzungaria was held is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: the Tarim Basin regained and the protectorate re-established (673-675)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. '673-675: Control of the oasis states returned to the Tang, and the protectorate was re-established.' The Anxi page does not date this return.

correction.text: the Tarim Basin without Qiuci, which the Tibetans captured in 677

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 677 the Tibetan Empire captured Qiuci.'

correction.text: the Tarim Basin and the Western Turkic lands after Pei Xingjian's victory of 679

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Pei Xingjian 'defeated Ashina Duzhi as well as the Tibetans and established control over the Western Regions'; Tokmak was annexed as a military base (Western Turks page).

correction.text: Xi Prefecture, Dzungaria and Semirechye after Tang troops left the Four Garrisons (686) and the Tibetans took the Western Regions (687)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 686 Tang troops withdrew from the Four Garrisons'; 'In 687 the Tibetan Empire established control over the Western Regions'; the Tibetans beat a Tang army at Issyk-Kul in 690, so Semirechye may have been lost too (the page does not say).

correction.text: the Western Regions pacified again by Wang Xiaojie, the protectorate re-established at Qiuci

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 692 Tang troops under Wang Xiaojie pacified the Western Regions and established the Anxi Protectorate at Qiuci' (with 30,000 Han soldiers, a note on the page).

correction.text: the Tarim Basin and Semirechye after Dzungaria, Turfan and Hami passed to the Beiting Protectorate

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 702 Wu Zetian set up the Beiting Protectorate in Ting Prefecture' and 'granted it governorship over Yi Prefecture'; it also governed Xi Prefecture. Ting, Yi and Xi are read as Dzungaria, Hami and Turfan.

correction.text: the Tarim Basin after the Turgesh captured Suiye (Suyab) in 719

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 719 the Turgesh captured Suiye.' The 755 withdrawal of '200,000 soldiers' and the 764 Tibetan cut-off of the Anxi and Beiting protectorates leave the Tarim in Tang hands on paper until 787.

correction.text: the Tarim Basin without Qiuci, conquered by the Tibetans in 787

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 787 the Tibetan Empire conquered Qiuci.'

correction.text: Yutian (Khotan), the last garrison, conquered in 792

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The last vestiges of the protectorate and its garrisons were defeated by Tibetan forces by 790'; 'In 792 the Tibetan Empire conquered Yutian.' Which oases survived between 790 and 792 is not stated; Khotan is the one the page names.

ledger.note: 640: the Anxi Protectorate is set up at Gaochang. 'On 19 September 640 Hou Junji of Tang conquered Gaochang and set up Xi Prefecture' and 'Xi Prefecture became the seat of the Anxi Protectorate on 11 October.'

region.text: Karasahr (Yanqi), the first of the Four Garrisons

ledger.note: 648: Karasahr is taken and garrisoned. 'In 648, the Tang conducted a second military campaign against Karasahr', setting up the first of the Four Garrisons of Anxi (the Tang dossier dates the annexation 644).
648: Kucha taken and made the seat. 'In 648, the Tang conquered Kucha, known to the Chinese as Qiuci, and made it the new seat of Anxi'; the Western Turks page has Kucha surrender on 19 January 649.

region.text: the Western Region, the Tarim oasis states

ledger.note: 650: the Tarim oases submit. 'By 650 the entire Western Region had submitted to Tang authority'; the Four Garrisons of Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar and Karasahr 'were installed between 648 and 658'. Khotan and Shule (Kashgar) had submitted as vassals in 632.
651: the seat goes back to Xi Prefecture (Gaochang); it returns to Qiuci in 658 after Su Dingfang's victory.

region.text: the Western Turkic lands north of the Tianshan and in the Chu and Ili valleys

ledger.note: 657: the Western Turkic lands. 'The khaganate was annexed after General Su Dingfang defeated Qaghan Ashina Helu in 657' and 'by the end of the 657 campaign, the Tang had reached its largest extent'; the page names neither Dzungaria nor Semirechye.
658: the seat returns to Qiuci (Kucha) 'after Su Dingfang defeated the Western Turkic Khaganate'.

region.text: Sogdia, Ferghana, Tashkent, Bukhara, Samarkand, Balkh, Herat, Tokharistan and Kabul

ledger.note: 659: the western states submit to the protectorate. The Sogdian, Ferghana, Tashkent, Bukhara, Samarkand, Balkh, Herat, Kashmir, Pamir, Tokharistan and Kabul states 'all submitted to the protectorate under Emperor Gaozong of Tang' in 659 (the Tang dossier has the same relation from 661).

region.text: the Four Garrisons in the Tarim Basin

ledger.note: 670: the Four Garrisons fall to Tibet. 'In 670 the Tibetan Empire routed a Tang army at the Battle of Dafei River' and took Qiuci; 'a Western Turkic tribe allied with the Tibetan Empire invaded the Tarim Basin' and the Tang 'withdrew to Turfan' (Western Turks page).
670: the seat moves to Suyab. 'The protectorate's seat was moved to Suyab, known as Suiye to the Chinese, in modern Kyrgyzstan.'

region.text: the oasis states of the Tarim Basin

ledger.note: 673-675: the Tarim is regained. 'Control of the oasis states returned to the Tang, and the protectorate was re-established'; the year is the start of the span.
677: Qiuci falls again. 'In 677 the Tibetan Empire captured Qiuci'; Ashina Duzhi revolted and proclaimed himself ruler of all Turks.

region.text: the Western Regions, the Four Garrisons

ledger.note: 679: Pei Xingjian restores the Western Regions. He 'defeated Ashina Duzhi as well as the Tibetans and established control over the Western Regions'; Tokmak was annexed as a base (Western Turks page).

region.text: the Four Garrisons and the Western Regions

ledger.note: 687: the Tarim goes to Tibet. 'In 686 Tang troops withdrew from the Four Garrisons' to save military spending; 'In 687 the Tibetan Empire established control over the Western Regions'; in 690 it beat a Tang army at Issyk-Kul.
692: Wang Xiaojie re-establishes the protectorate. 'Tang troops under Wang Xiaojie pacified the Western Regions and established the Anxi Protectorate at Qiuci' with 30,000 Han soldiers.
692: the seat is Qiuci, 'where it would remain until the protectorate's demise around 790'.

region.text: Ting, Yi and Xi prefectures: Dzungaria, Hami and Turfan

ledger.note: 702: the Beiting Protectorate is cut out. 'Wu Zetian set up the Beiting Protectorate in Ting Prefecture' and 'granted it governorship over Yi Prefecture'; it also governed Xi Prefecture, so Dzungaria, Hami and Turfan pass from the Anxi to the Beiting.
719: Suyab falls. 'In 719 the Turgesh captured Suiye', the former seat; the Chu and Ili valleys won in 657 go with it.

region.text: Transoxania, where the Tang presence ended

ledger.note: 751: Talas ends the western vassalage. 'In 751 Tang forces suffered a major defeat at the Battle of Talas against Abbasid and Karluk forces'; the Tang dossier dates the end of the Tang presence in Transoxania to July 751.
787: Qiuci is lost for good. 'In 787 the Tibetan Empire conquered Qiuci.'

790: the garrisons fall. 'The last vestiges of the protectorate and its garrisons were defeated by Tibetan forces by 790', 'ending nearly 150 years of Tang influence in Central Asia'; the page names only Khotan as holding out to 792.

792: Yutian falls. 'In 792 the Tibetan Empire conquered Yutian' (Khotan); of the four garrisons 'all eventually ended up freeing themselves': Karasahr and Kucha to the Qocho (843), Kashgar to the Kara-Khanids, Khotan independent in 851.

wars.name: Tang conquest of the Tarim and the Western Turks

zones.text: Gaochang 640, Karasahr and Kucha 648-649, the Western Turkic lands 657

wars.outcome: Tang victory: the Four Garrisons of Anxi in 648-658 and, after Su Dingfang beat Ashina Helu in 657, the largest extent.
wars.note: Gaochang 19 September 640; Karasahr 648; Kucha surrendered 19 January 649; the khaganate annexed 657.

wars.name: Tang-Tibetan wars for the Western Regions
wars.outcome: Tibet took the Four Garrisons in 670, 677 and 686-687; Pei Xingjian regained them in 679 and Wang Xiaojie in 692.
wars.note: 670 Dafei River; 677 Qiuci; 679 Pei Xingjian; 686 withdrawal; 687 Tibet in control; 690 Issyk-Kul; 692 Wang Xiaojie.

wars.name: Turgesh, Arab and Tibetan pressure on Anxi
wars.outcome: The Turgesh captured Suiye in 719; Tibet raided Fergana (715), Gumo and the Stone City (717, 720, 741); Tang recovered the Stone City in 749 and lost at Talas against Abbasid and Karluk forces in 751.
wars.note: Only the 719 loss moves a border in the ledger.

wars.name: Tibetan conquest of the Tarim
wars.outcome: After 764 cut off the Anxi and Beiting protectorates from China, Tibet conquered Qiuci (787), the last garrisons ('by 790') and Yutian (792).
wars.note: The 755 withdrawal of 200,000 soldiers from the Western Regions to defend the capital is the page's background.

certainty.note: Oasis and steppe frontiers, never surveyed on the pages opened; the Tarim, Semirechye and Dzungaria shapes are named regions, not boundaries.

sources.title: Protectorate General to Pacify the West
sources.note: Seats and dates 640-792, Four Garrisons, the 659 submissions, Tibetan swings 670-692, Beiting 702, Turgesh 719, Talas 751, 764, 787, 790, 792.

sources.title: Tang campaigns against the Western Turks
sources.note: Karasahr 648, Kucha 19 January 649, 657 annexation and largest extent, 670 withdrawal, 673-675 return, 679 Tokmak.

notes: Written for ea-04-x on the pattern of the Andong protectorate dossier (type colony). The Tang dossier already carries the same land as direct Tang gains and losses (648, 657, 670, 673-679, 687, 692, 719, 787, 790, 792) and as vassal events; this dossier adds the protectorate as an internal unit with its own seat and extent, so a reviewer should decide whether the renderer draws the Tang tint under it. Open points: (1) the Beiting Protectorate (702-790) is written as its own dossier (beiting-protectorate); (2) the Tang dossier dates Karasahr 644 and Kucha 648, this page 648 and 648-649; (3) the Anxi page gives no dates for Dzungaria or Semirechye, which are the researcher's reading of 657; (4) Issyk-Kul in 690 may have cost Semirechye but no page says so; (5) the 790 shrink to Khotan is confidence 2 because the page names no surviving oasis but Yutian; (6) vassal pair 659-751 uses the Tang dossier's counterpart string for the Sogdian and Tokharistan states.
